Debarment

Debarment is one of the most serious consequences in financial services.

Debarment is one of the most serious consequences in financial services. Let us work through what it means, when it may apply, how the process works and what the consequences are.

As a Representative or Key Individual, you are expected to meet ongoing Fit and Proper requirements and uphold the standards expected within the financial services industry. When these standards are not met, there may be serious consequences.

In this lesson, you'll learn what debarment is, why it happens, and how it can affect an individual's ability to work in the financial services industry. Let's explore the standards of conduct expected of you and the role debarment plays in protecting Customers and maintaining trust in the industry.

What is Debarment?

Debarment is a formal process whereby a Key Individual or Representative is prevented from rendering financial services in the future where they have either:

  • Contravened one or more provisions of FAIS or its regulations.
  • No longer meet the Fit and Proper Requirements for Financial Services Providers.
  • TFG has a Debarment Policy that details:
  • TFG's obligations when initiating a debarment process.
  • Your rights if you are subject to a debarment process.

You are required to familiarise yourself with this policy and understand the consequences debarment may have on your future career in financial services.

When are you at risk of Debarment?

You may be at risk of debarment if you contravene one or more provisions of FAIS and its regulations.

Common examples include:

  • Dishonesty, fraud, or misrepresentation.
  • Failure to disclose conflicts of interest.
  • Unauthorised rendering of financial services.
Maintaining Fit and Proper Status

You may also be at risk of debarment if you fail to continuously meet the Fit and Proper requirements.

These requirements include:

  • Personal character qualities of honesty and integrity.
  • Good standing.
  • Competence.
  • Continuous Professional Development (CPD).
  • Operational ability.
  • Financial soundness.

TFG's Debarment Policy provides practical examples of what non-compliance with these requirements may look like.

How Does the Debarment Process Work?

Review the process below to understand how a debarment matter may be managed.

Debarment is a formal process and must be conducted fairly while ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements.

1

Potential Non-Compliance Identified

A potential contravention of FAIS requirements or Fit and Proper standards is identified.

2

Notice of Intention to Debar

TFG provides written notice which includes:

  • Formal notification of TFG's intention to debar.
  • The reasons for the proposed debarment.
  • Any conditions that may be attached to the debarment.
  • Measures designed to protect Customer interests.
  • A copy of TFG's Debarment Policy.
3

Opportunity to Respond

The affected individual is provided with a reasonable opportunity to make a submission. For example, 30 days may be allowed for a response.

4

Assessment of the Information

TFG will consider:

  • The individual's response.
  • Available evidence.
  • Information from an Ombudsman.
  • Information from the FSCA where applicable.
5

Hearing (Where Applicable)

TFG may, at its discretion, facilitate a debarment hearing involving the affected parties and management. The hearing may be coordinated with employment-related disciplinary proceedings in accordance with the TFG Disciplinary Policy.

6

Decision

A decision is made based on all available information.

7

Written Notification

The individual is informed of the decision in writing. This notification must also include information regarding the individual's right to appeal the decision through the Financial Services Tribunal.

Important to Remember
  • A person may be debarred while employed by TFG.
  • A person may also be debarred for conduct that occurred during employment for up to six months after employment has ended.
  • A person may also be debarred directly by the FSCA on the same grounds.

Consequences of Debarment

Select each tab to explore the consequences of debarment.

Immediate Consequences

When a person is debarred:

  • They are no longer authorised to act on behalf of TFG.
  • They must immediately stop all related financial services activities.
  • They are removed from the Representative Register.
  • TFG notifies the FSCA of the debarment and the reasons for it.

Future Employment Impact

Once debarred:

  • The individual may not be appointed as a Representative or Key Individual at TFG.
  • The individual may not be appointed as a Representative or Key Individual at another Financial Services Provider.

Reappointment is only possible through an application to the FSCA.

Reappointment and Rehabilitation

Applications for reappointment generally require:

  • A minimum debarment period of 12 months.
  • Evidence that the individual has been rehabilitated.
  • Evidence of reform and a permanent change in behaviour.
  • Demonstration that the individual can act in the best interests of Customers and meet the industry's integrity standards.

In some circumstances, such as qualification-related Fit and Proper contraventions, reappointment may be considered once the required qualification has been obtained, even if the 12-month period has not yet elapsed.

Knowledge Check

James is a Representative at TFG Insure. During an investigation, it is discovered that she intentionally failed to disclose a conflict of interest and provided inaccurate information about the relationship. Which outcome could this lead to?

Correct. Debarment may occur when a Representative or Key Individual no longer meets the Fit and Proper requirements, including the honesty and integrity standards required by FAIS. Failing to disclose a conflict of interest or providing inaccurate information may result in debarment.

Not quite. Debarment is not limited to situations where Customers suffer a loss. Representatives and Key Individuals must continuously meet the Fit and Proper requirements, including maintaining honesty and integrity. Failure to disclose conflicts of interest, dishonesty, fraud, misrepresentation, or failing to meet Fit and Proper requirements may all result in debarment.

Key Takeaway

You now understand that debarment is a serious regulatory consequence. It may apply when a Representative or Key Individual contravenes FAIS requirements or no longer meets the ongoing Fit and Proper requirements. Throughout this course, you have considered how your knowledge, decisions, and conduct contribute to fair Customer outcomes and regulatory compliance.

Before you finish, take a moment to bring everything together and reflect on how you will apply these principles in your role.
